name: Intel FlexRAN
what_it_is: Intel's 4G and 5G baseband PHY reference design that runs on Xeon processors using Intel Architecture. It provides a validated L1 binary implementation for 5G NR Layer 1 signal processing, tested on SkyLake and CascadeLake platforms.
components: l1app — L1 application that processes baseband PHY signals
testmac — testing framework that exercises PHY APIs and generates/compares IQ samples
oran-fapi — FAPI interface layer between L1 and upper layers
DPDK BBDev — data-plane library used for both software FEC and FPGA/ASIC FEC offload
Software FEC SDK — Intel FEC library for in-CPU forward error correction
protocols: Proprietary private interface between L1 and testmac
measurement: IQ sample comparison for DL/UL/full-duplex producing pass/fail reports
cyclictest latency measurements in microseconds on isolated CPU cores
Per-slot test run results via XML configuration files
PUSCH, PUCCH, PRACH, and SRS channel-level validation
configuration: XML configuration files for multi-slot test scenarios
BIOS settings: CPU power policy, frequency scaling, C-states
OS kernel parameters for real-time tuning
CPU frequency management via MSR tools
FEC mode selection: software (DPDK BBDev + SDK) or FPGA/ASIC offload
Kubernetes resource manifests with hugepage and memory limits per container
modes: FD — full duplex (combined DL and UL)
constraints: Requires Intel Xeon SkyLake or CascadeLake processor; no support documented for other CPU families
Hugepages mandatory: l1app needs 2Gi, oran-fapi needs 4Gi hugepages allocated at host level
Real-time OS tuning (isolated CPUs, C-state disabling, frequency pinning) required for valid latency results
FEC must run either fully in-CPU via DPDK BBDev+SDK or fully offloaded to FPGA/ASIC — mixed mode not documented
Distributed as validated L1 binaries, not source code; no rebuild or cross-compilation supported
notable_absences: No fault injection or error-injection framework documented
No explicit latency budgets or throughput targets published in the README
No scalability limits (max UEs, max cells) documented
No docker-compose file found; deployment described via Kubernetes manifests only
Source code not provided — only pre-compiled binaries
